title: Overdrive insights response
description: The answer to GET /v1/insights?from&to (spec §6.5, §6.6, §12.3, §8.3, ADR 0025): the written notes whose createdAt falls on a local day (TIMEZONE) from `from` to `to`, both included, at most 366 days (400 invalid_range otherwise), newest first (createdAt, then id, descending). kind is morning (state, why, what to do with today's workout: a recommendation in words, never a plan change), ride (how a ride went against its plan; its rideId is set), week (the weekly review), deviation (a metric outside the rider's own baseline for several days in a row, with a plain reading of what that usually means for training) or drift (missed sessions, or load far from the plan). text is plain text of one to a few short paragraphs, written from facts the service computed (by a language model, checked by code so that it quotes only numbers that were supplied, or by a deterministic template when no model is configured or its text was rejected); it never carries a diagnosis and names no medical condition. rideId is the ride a ride note is about and is null for every other kind. topic is the discussion topic the ride note carries (discussion-topic.schema.json) or null; only ride notes have one, and its rideId is the note's. Every answer carries generatedAt (when the service built it) and stale, which is false: notes are read from the service's own database, so nothing they depend on can be out of date. Rules a schema cannot state, checked by every implementation: from and to are real calendar dates, from is not after to and the range is at most 366 days; generatedAt and every createdAt are real UTC instants; a note's id is unique in the answer; the notes are ordered newest first; rideId is set exactly for kind ride; topic is null unless kind is ride, and then topic.rideId equals rideId.
